verdict.rationale: Apple's own materials show a first-party developer stack built around Apple silicon: Xcode builds and simulators, the Metal 4 shader compiler and Metal debugger for profiling and optimizing, PyTorch backends, and the MLX framework designed for Apple silicon. That points to tier-one ecosystem treatment, but the pack never documents general-purpose compiler maturity or architecture-specific optimization guidance for M4 Max. missing for 10: evidence of mature CPU compiler toolchains (clang/LLVM, other languages), official M4/Apple-silicon CPU optimization guides, explicit OS/toolchain tier-one support statements, and independent developer corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, this architecture is a first-class development target — mature compilers, official optimization guidance, and an OS and tooling ecosystem that treats it as tier one

citations.quote: This huge boost in performance makes building and testing apps across multiple simulators in Xcode quicker than ever.
Inspect, debug, and optimize your entire rendering pipeline with Metal debugger — from mesh shading to ray tracing and machine learning.
Metal 4 enables entirely new ways to integrate machine learning while also enabling you to encode commands and compile shaders more efficiently than ever.
MLX is an array framework for machine learning on Apple silicon, brought to you by Apple machine learning research.
Accelerate the training of machine learning models in third-party frameworks right on your Mac with PyTorch backends.
